issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) specifies addGuestStudents(int): void, and the solution implements public void addGuestStudents(int). However the template defines a different signature: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). This parameter mismatch between template and both the specification and solution is structural: students following the exercise text will implement addGuestStudents(int) but find a template stub with an extra boolean parameter, which is likely to confuse them and break automated tests or expected usage.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template method signature match the specification and the solution: replace the template stub with public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO: implement */ }. Alternatively, if the boolean parameter was intentional, update the problem statement and solution to document and use addGuestStudents(int, boolean) consistently. Prefer the first option to preserve the current exercise description and solution.
